Assistant: Found it — line 216: `VideoPlayer(player: AVPlayer(url: first))`. The `AVPlayer` is constructed **inline inside the view's `body`**, so every single SwiftUI re-render (any state change, scroll, parent update) creates a brand-new `AVPlayer`/`AVPlayerViewController` from scratch, tearing down and rebuilding all its KVO observers each time. That's exactly the profile signature. Let's look at the surrounding view.

Assistant: This is the real, serious bug: `mediaGroup(urls:kind:)` runs on every SwiftUI body re-evaluation, and constructs a brand-new `AVPlayer` (and thus a brand-new underlying `AVPlayerViewController` with full KVO setup) every single time — regardless of whether the video URL changed. Any note with a video pays this cost on *every* re-render, not once. Let me check imports, then fix it properly by hoisting the player into `@State` so it's created exactly once per view identity.

Assistant: `AVKit` already imported (brings both `AVPlayer` and `VideoPlayer`). Now applying the fix.

Assistant: Good — one-component-per-file is the established convention here. Creating `NostrInlineVideoPlayer.swift` following that pattern. [...] **Root cause of the "completely unresponsive" 3.5-minute freeze, found by profiling the actual pegged process (not guessed):** `NostrContentView.swift:216` — `VideoPlayer(player: AVPlayer(url: first))` constructed the `AVPlayer` **inline inside the view's `body`**. SwiftUI re-evaluates `body` on every scroll, every unrelated state change, every live timestamp refresh — anything. Each re-evaluation tore down and rebuilt the entire `AVPlayerViewController`, including a full KVO observer registration/deregistration pass. Profiled live: this was eating **65% of main-thread samples** in a 5-second window, which is exactly what "completely unresponsive" looks like — the main thread, not a background worker, was saturated.

**Fix:** moved the `AVPlayer` into a dedicated view (`NostrInlineVideoPlayer.swift`) with `@State`, so it's constructed exactly once per view identity instead of on every re-render.
